newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco court case against Massachusetts postponed.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco court case against Massachusetts postponed.

text.p: A federal court hearing challenging a proposed Massachusetts law to force tobacco companies to disclose their ingredients and comply with stronger nicotine ratings scheduled for Tuesday has been postponed, the state's attorney general's office said.
No future date has been set for the case, a spokeswoman said.

Four tobacco comapanies -- Philip Morris Cos Inc, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc and Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp -- have challenged the proposed law.
The companies said the law would reveal their trade secrets and pre-empt federal laws covering tobacco.
Scheduled to go into effect next July, the law would be the first in the country to force the companies to reveal their ingredients.
